selected researchall 9 →

  • 2026-10-05 — agents / formal verification Verified once, reused three times: agents carried proofs of shipped OpenSSL code into new callers Machine-checked contracts for two unchanged Debian OpenSSL routines verified three experimental callers through their actual linkage. The held-out caller missed its three-hour cap, then completed in a recorded successor.
  • 2026-09-27 — agents / formal verification Agents turned a one-kernel Lean proof into a checker that certified 25 PyTorch kernels One Lean theorem and a small checker certified 32-bit size arguments for 25 torch.compile kernels, including 10 of 24 held out, with each proof bound to the live compilation. Two of nine tuned kernels got faster.
  • 2026-09-26 — agents / formal verification A Lean proof let agents cut a compiled PyTorch workload’s runtime by 26% Agents declared a torch.compile kernel’s size arguments 32-bit, proved in Lean when that is exact, and cut a changing-shape workload’s time by 26% on one L4. The opt-in patch is an open PyTorch PR.
  • 2026-09-25 — agents / formal verification 25 bugs in free-threaded CPython, found by agents Agents confirmed 25 bugs in the no-GIL build, with no earlier report found for 18. TLAPS and Lean proofs of the locking model held; replays of real runs showed five places CPython leaves it.
  • 2026-09-24 — agents / formal verification I used formal verification and agents to make an algorithm 105× faster and prove it behaves the same Claude Opus 5.5 rewrote four deliberately slow Dafny routines under a frozen spec it could not edit. Seven rewrites verified, and one ran 105× faster on a workload it never saw.
  • 2026-05-26 — rl / sampling bias A 50-step RL update reduces categorical sampling bias Fifty RL steps on one random-integer task moved nine untrained pick-one tasks toward uniform on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct.
  • 2026-04-25 — interp / probes Hidden-state probes outperform self-reported confidence A linear probe on Llama 3.1 8B’s hidden states ranks claim correctness better than the model’s stated confidence.

selected softwareall 30 →

  • Pith

    A Dafny-verified application core that a coding agent builds an application around, with a judge that says which properties of the result are proved, model-checked, tested, or awaiting human review. Research prototype.

    Needs: Dafny 4.11 · TLC · Python, installed by bootstrap.sh · v0.4.1 release

    agent contract · validation record · release v0.4.1 · source

  • HN, formally

    The Hacker News front page, rendered by a Lean 4 program proven to render every API input correctly and redesigned every night by an LLM loop that ships without human review. Layout and accessibility are checked per release, never called proven.

    Needs: Nothing to install: hosted on GitHub Pages · Lean 4.34 and Node 22 to build

    live site · every generation · latest release · source

  • Faithful

    Make one TypeScript function faster and see exactly how much of “it still does the same thing” was checked: compile, purity, differential tests, a bounded Z3 search, a benchmark, then a Lean 4 proof against an agreed spec. In the launch campaign, 3 of 130 candidate rewrites were accepted with a proof.

    Needs: Node 22.12+ · pnpm · Codex CLI · Lean 4 and Mathlib (about 12 GB) for proofs · Z3 optional · install from source, 0.1.0

    try it in your browser · launch report · source

  • Undefined

    Ask a question of a spreadsheet export. A model drafts the calculation and the checks it must pass, you approve the checks, and only an answer that clears a strict TypeScript compiler, unit and property tests, and purity and time-limit gates is shown. Also a CLI and GitHub Action that certify TypeScript from any source.

    Needs: Nothing to install for the demo (recorded gpt-6-luna answers, live checks) · a local copy needs Node 20.19+ and the Codex CLI · install from source, 0.1.0

    try it in your browser · how the checks are measured · source

  • Dynamic Workflows on Codex

    A Claude Code skill that writes a multi-agent workflow script, runs it on Codex agents instead of Claude subagents, and shows the run as a live map. Agents edit files without asking unless the run is read-only.

    Needs: Node 18+ · logged-in Codex CLI · Claude Code plugin or standalone CLI, v0.2.0 release

    install · offline demo · release v0.2.0 · source

  • Flightdeck

    A Claude Code mod that puts a live agent dashboard in your terminal: context and cost, every permission check, your subagents as cards or swimlanes. It only watches.

    Needs: Claude Code 2.1.287+ · install as a plugin · v0.3.2 release

    install · what it can reach · release v0.3.2 · source
